implementation.summary: New internal buildPrompt(frozen, nodeIdFor) in core/payload — 32 lines, no new types, no builder, no state. Singular/plural headline with NO screen clause (orchestrator decision: the design's 'on the Cart screen' names the design demo's own app and this codebase has no screen-name source, so fabricating one would inject invented data into every prompt sent to Claude; hierarchy.xml carries the real context). Device line derived from frozen.deviceLabel + frozen.deviceSize, never the design's hardcoded literal — the frozen test deliberately uses different numbers so a hardcoded impl fails. Per annotation: '#{index} [{nodeId} · ]{w}×{h}' with the node-id segment AND its separator both dropped via listOfNotNull when nodeIdFor returns null, then the comment three-space-indented and quoted verbatim ('no comment' when empty), then a blank line. NO 'measured:' branch: core/measure's noteLine already folds the measurement into the comment as a ⌥-prefixed line, which passes through byte-identical. Trailer 'Attached: frame.png, N crops, hierarchy.xml'. Joined with newlines, no trailing newline.

troubleshooting.issue: linkReleaseFrameworkIosArm64 plus two linkReleaseFrameworkIosSimulatorArm64 tasks failed with 'e: Compilation failed: Java heap space' / OutOfMemoryError under four concurrent release links. This is the same flake wave 2 hit with no diagnostic — now with a visible root cause.
troubleshooting.resolution: Re-ran the identical command once with no code change: BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Not a code defect and NOT fixed — the Kotlin/Native release linker simply exhausts heap at this parallelism. Needs a gradle/native daemon heap bump or a serialized release link in an infra task; logged as a Stage 7 reflection candidate because it affects every future cross-target gate in this repo.

troubleshooting.issue: The brief specified the badge as '#{i+1}' (list position); the implementer used StagedAnnotation.index instead.
troubleshooting.resolution: ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED AND ACCEPTED: deleteAnnotation renumbers survivors via annotation.copy(index = position + 1) (MirrorViewModel.kt:518-520), so index == position+1 is an invariant rather than a coincidence of the fixtures. The two can never disagree, so there is no inconsistency risk against the crop captions (which use list position), and index is the field that matches the badge painted on the frame.
